events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 309 PM EDT, Emergency management reported thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Anderson, Noblesville, Elwood, Tipton, Windfall, Westfield,
Cicero, Pendleton, Sheridan, Chesterfield, Lapel, Edgewood,
Frankton, Arcadia, Atlanta, Sharpsville, Markleville, Kempton,
Woodlawn Heights and Country Club Heights.

This includes Interstate 69 between mile markers 215 and 230.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Keokuk; Washington; Louisa; Jefferson; Henry; Des Moines; Van Buren; Lee; Mercer; Henderson; Warren; Hancock; McDonough; Scotland; Clark
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Illinois, including the following areas,
Hancock, Henderson, McDonough, Mercer and Warren, southeast Iowa,
including the following areas, Des Moines, Henry IA, Jefferson,
Keokuk, Lee, Louisa, Van Buren and Washington, and northeast
Missouri, including the following areas, Clark and Scotland.

* WHEN...Through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Some of the
flooding may significant.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rounds of rain with embedded thunderstorms will occur across the
area through Saturday morning with peak hourly rates between 1 to
2 inches from the strongest storms. Rainfall totals will vary
considerably across the watch area. The hardest hit areas north
of Highway 34 could receive 5 to 8 inches of rainfall with
isolated higher amounts possible. Flash flooding is a risk with
an increased probability of river and creek flooding.
